moat_against: Commodity price-taker: ammonia, urea, UAN and AN are undifferentiated; price is set globally, CF has no pricing power
Earnings hostage to the nitrogen price / natural gas spread — revenue went $11.186B (FY2022) to $5.936B (FY2024) in two years
Cost advantage can narrow if U.S. gas rises or European/Asian gas falls; new global capacity (incl. CF's own Blue Point, ~$2B CF share, 2029) adds supply
Concentration and outage risk: Yazoo City complex (up to 1.3M tons) idled since Nov 2025, restart pushed to H1 2027; Q2 2026 sales volume fell 15.3% YoY
Capex intensity rising: TTM capex $1.067B vs $0.453-0.518B/yr in FY2022-FY2024, funding Blue Point and the Yazoo rebuild
moat_for: Low-cost North American natural gas feedstock (Henry Hub/AECO) vs European/Asian rivals on high-cost imported LNG — gas is 70-90% of nitrogen cash cost
Scale and operating excellence: ~98% of available ammonia capacity utilized in H1 2026 vs ~86% North American peer benchmark
Mississippi River, pipeline and rail logistics network from Gulf Coast plants (Donaldsonville) into the U.S. Corn Belt
ROIC proxy above 20% in each of FY2023-FY2025 and positive through the FY2020 trough (9.4%)
Disciplined capital return: diluted shares fell from 216.2M (FY2021) to 162.2M (FY2025) to 154.2M current-YTD (ttm.py); dividend raised 20% to $0.60/qtr in July 2026
moat_justification: Structural low-cost position from North American Henry Hub / AECO natural gas (70-90% of nitrogen production cost) versus European/Asian rivals on imported LNG, plus scale, 98% ammonia capacity utilization in H1 2026 vs an ~86% North American peer benchmark, and a Mississippi River / pipeline logistics network into the Corn Belt — against pure commodity price-taker economics: undifferentiated nitrogen products, no pricing power, earnings set by the global nitrogen price and the gas spread. ROIC proxy was strong in the last five fiscal years (28.0% in FY2021, 73.3% in FY2022, 27.4% in FY2023, 23.1% in FY2024, 30.4% in FY2025 in fundamentals.json) but that history is cycle-inflated — the FY2022 spike and a 9.4% trough in FY2020 show the returns are spread-driven, not franchise-driven — and gross margin swung from 19.4% (FY2020) to 52.4% (FY2022) to 34.6% (FY2024) to 38.5% (FY2025). A cost moat that pays only when the spread is wide is moderate, not wide: 5/10.
name: CF Industries Holdings, Inc.
one_liner: Low-cost North American nitrogen producer with a real gas-spread cost moat but commodity price-taker earnings, moat 5/10 — at $120.85 the TTM-base DCF yields a 14.7% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $118.16 (Tier C, bear-to-bull band C to B); it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$118, essentially today's price with no margin of safety against nitrogen-price normalization.
